evidence_notes: No representative cases are assigned to this candidate boundary.

The source_shape field acknowledges only one webhook URL validator case and one general HTTP address-policy case, neither of which is sufficient to establish webhook/callback dispatch as a shared released boundary.

The safe_fix_semantics field describes what fix evidence would be needed (destination validation, allowlisting, private-range blocking, parser-consistent checks, redirect-hop validation), but none of this evidence is present.
The exploit_precondition and sink_or_sensitive_effect fields are phrased as aspirational requirements rather than observed evidence.
main_issue: The boundary describes a conceptually coherent mechanism (webhook/callback SSRF) but has zero representative cases and zero evidence refs. The source_shape, sink_or_sensitive_effect, exploit_precondition, and safe_fix_semantics fields all describe what would be needed, not what exists. There is no case-level evidence to evaluate whether the claimed mechanism actually binds the group together.
mechanism_name: attacker-controlled webhook or callback URL fetch

evidence_notes: bugsink__bugsink::CVE-2026-44502: Parser-boundary mismatch — urllib.parse.urlparse used for scheme/hostname decisions before outbound policy checks; patch switches to requests preparation + urllib3 parsing and rejects raw non-RFC characters. Source evidence confirms the gap is in the parser used to validate the URL before dispatch.

cc-tweaked__cc-tweaked::CVE-2023-37262: Incomplete deny-list range coverage — PrivatePattern.matches checked any-local, loopback, link-local, site-local but omitted cloud metadata addresses and multicast ranges. Source evidence confirms the gap is in the address-range predicate, not in URL parsing.

Both cases support 'attacker-influenced outbound destination + incomplete destination constraint' as the shared mechanism. The boundary text's parser-inconsistency clause (scheme, host parsing, DNS/IP resolution, private/loopback/link-local/multicast/cloud-metadata ranges, redirect hops, parser inconsistencies) covers both sub-variants.

Coverage is thin at n=2 cases. The mechanism is broad enough to cover more cases, but the current evidence only supports two distinct sub-variants. Consider adding more cases across both parser-boundary and range-coverage variants to strengthen the boundary.
main_issue: Two cases share a genuine common mechanism (server-side outbound URL with incomplete destination policy), but the specific gap flavor differs: Bugsink is a parser-boundary mismatch (urlparse vs. urllib3/requests), while CC-Tweaked is missing address ranges (cloud-metadata, multicast). The boundary text abstracts these into 'incomplete effective destination policy' which holds, but the two cases represent different sub-variants within the same mechanism family. Coverage is limited at n=2.
mechanism_name: server-side outbound URL request with incomplete destination policy
